title: Alamance County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Alamance County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Alamance County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Alamance County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from North Carolina statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Alamance County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Alamance County

  • Alamance County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Alamance County?
We buy Alamance County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How to sell a house in Alamance County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Alamance County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Alamance County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Alamance County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Alamance County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Alamance County register of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Alamance County?

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe real estate transfer tax?

Real estate transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue explains the rule.

The Chatham County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Chatham County

  • Chatham County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • E-recording accepted Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., including plats; vendors Simplifile and CSC (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Chatham County?
We buy Chatham County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How to sell a house in Chatham County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Chatham County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Chatham County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Chatham County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

title: Currituck County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Currituck County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Currituck County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Currituck County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from North Carolina statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Currituck County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Currituck County

  • Currituck County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Fees: $26 pages 1-15, $4 each additional; Deed of Trust $64 pages 1-35; $25 additional DT reference; $10 each additional instrument; satisfaction first reference $0
  • Address 153 Courthouse Road, Currituck, NC; Mon-Fri 8:00 AM-5:00 PM
  • Excise stamp tax $1.00 per $500 of consideration

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Currituck County?
We buy Currituck County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How to sell a house in Currituck County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Currituck County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Currituck County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Currituck County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Currituck County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Currituck County register of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Currituck County?

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe real estate transfer tax?

Real estate transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue explains the rule.

The Edgecombe County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Edgecombe County

  • Edgecombe County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Edgecombe County?
We buy Edgecombe County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

  • Current-year due/interest dates on county page

  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Edgecombe County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Edgecombe County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Who records deeds in Lee County

  • Lee County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Recording and transfer tax

  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)

  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

We buy Lee County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Lee County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Lee County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.

  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Who records deeds in Richmond County

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Office hours 8:00-5:00; recording hours 8:00-4:30; e-recording hours 8 AM-4:00 PM; fee schedule on page (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Franklin St, Room 101, Rockingham NC 28379 (RoD FAQ, vendor-hosted) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

We buy Richmond County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Richmond County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Richmond County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.

  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

title: Rutherford County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Rutherford County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Rutherford County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Rutherford County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from North Carolina statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Rutherford County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Rutherford County

  • Rutherford County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • 229 N. Main St., Suite 202A, Rutherfordton, NC 28139; PO Box 551; hours 8:30-5:00 Mon-Fri (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • eRecording in office since April 24, 2018 via Simplifile; plat eRecording since Feb 1, 2022 (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Rutherford County?
We buy Rutherford County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How to sell a house in Rutherford County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Rutherford County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Rutherford County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Rutherford County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Rutherford County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Rutherford County register of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Rutherford County?

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe real estate transfer tax?

Real estate transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue explains the rule.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from North Carolina statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Watauga County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Watauga County

  • Watauga County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

What we confirmed on the official page

  • Electronic recording page lists 814 W. King Street, Boone, NC 28607 and eRecording vendor contact numbers (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Certified copy $10 plus $14 state vital records fee when ordered via state service (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Watauga County?
We buy Watauga County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Due date and interest terms on Watauga page

How to sell a house in Watauga County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Watauga County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Watauga County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Watauga County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Watauga County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Where do I record a deed in Watauga County?

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe real estate transfer tax?

Real estate transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue explains the rule.

Yadkin County, NC Register of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Yadkin County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Yadkin County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from North Carolina statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

The Yadkin County register of deeds records North Carolina deeds and mortgages. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who records deeds in Yadkin County

  • Yadkin County Register of Deeds records deeds and mortgages.

Recording and transfer tax

  • Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value. (N.C.G.S. 105-228.30(a); source)
  • Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1); source)
  • Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page. (N.C.G.S. 161-10(a)(1a); source)

Fees

County recording fees change, so we do not quote a total. Check the recorder's current fee schedule before you file.

Selling in Yadkin County?
We buy Yadkin County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Current-year due/interest dates
  • Recording fee amounts and hours
  • Board of Equalization and Review dates

How to sell a house in Yadkin County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. North Carolina closings run through an attorney, and for an inherited or transferred house that means the recorded deed or the estate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in North Carolina.

What a cash sale of a Yadkin County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Yadkin County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required North Carolina disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Yadkin County

  • Ask the county recorder what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in North Carolina change, so confirm details with the official office or a North Carolina attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Yadkin County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Yadkin County register of deeds FAQ

Where do I record a deed in Yadkin County?

With the Register of Deeds. Confirm submission rules on the county page.

Do I owe real estate transfer tax?

Real estate transfer tax can apply to deeds. The Department of Revenue explains the rule.
